articles.title: Man and woman arrested over Waterford arson attack
articles.rewritten_copy:
ARSON HORROR: FOUR DEAD, TWO KIDS FIGHTING FOR LIFE IN WATERFORD INFERNO

A man and woman are behind bars in connection with the devastating arson attack that ripped through a home in Waterford city, leaving four innocent people dead and two young children clinging to life. The pair, a man in his 20s and a woman in her 30s, are being held under tough anti-gang laws, accused of facilitating a criminal organisation.

Gardaí are working tirelessly to get to the bottom of this heinous crime, with the investigation team appealing for anyone with information to come forward. The community is in shock after the brutal attack, which saw a family torn apart in the most horrific way imaginable. As the people of Waterford struggle to come to terms with this senseless tragedy, one thing is clear: justice must be served.

articles.title: Donaldson given 15-year sentence for rape, sexual assault
articles.rewritten_copy:
JUSTICE FINALLY SERVED: DONALDSON CAGED FOR SICKENING ABUSE OF SCHOOLGIRLS

Former DUP leader Jeffrey Donaldson has been handed a 15-year sentence for the horrific rape and sexual assault of two young schoolgirls, spanning over two decades. However, in a move that will raise eyebrows, Donaldson will only spend seven and a half years behind bars due to an automatic 50% remission of his sentence. Judge Paul Ramsey slammed Donaldson's behaviour, saying it had led to a "catastrophic descent into disgrace". The victims, who were just primary school age at the time, have been left with permanent scars, with one saying she had been "broken" by the abuse.

The sentencing has been welcomed by the Public Prosecution Service, with Catherine Kierans praising the courage of the two complainants and encouraging other victims of sexual abuse to come forward. The PSNI has also commended the bravery of the women, saying Donaldson "manipulated and exploited" them for his own twisted gain. As the people of Northern Ireland struggle to come to terms with the shocking fall from grace of a former leader, one thing is clear: justice has finally been served, but the question remains - is seven and a half years behind bars enough for such heinous crimes?

articles.title: 'My childhood was stolen from me', says abuse survivor
articles.rewritten_copy:
DONALDSON'S DARKEST DEEDS: DUP LEADER'S VICTIMS SPEAK OUT AFTER JAILING

The disgusting crimes of former DUP leader Jeffrey Donaldson have left two young lives in tatters, as his victims broke their silence to reveal the devastating impact of his rape and sexual assault. The trial heard that Donaldson's offending spanned over two decades, from 1985 to 2008, leaving his victims to pick up the pieces of their shattered childhoods.

In heart-wrenching victim impact statements, the two survivors, who were just primary school age when the abuse began, spoke of the lasting effects of Donaldson's actions. One victim said she wished she could have grown up like other children, without feeling "ashamed and dirty", while the other revealed that her experience had affected "every day and every relationship" she had ever had.

The victims' brave words are a stark reminder of the need for justice and accountability for those who commit such heinous crimes. As one victim so eloquently put it, "the cycle is being broken and it ends with me" - a testament to the strength and resilience of those who have suffered at the hands of Donaldson.

articles.title: Trump says gunman's execution will not be livestreamed
articles.rewritten_copy:
TRUMP PULLS PLUG ON LIVE EXECUTION FEED

In a surprise U-turn, US President Donald Trump has scrapped plans to livestream the execution of Fort Hood gunman Nidal Hasan. The move follows widespread outrage from politicians, rights groups, and the public, with many slamming the proposal as gratuitous and unnecessary. 

Hasan, a former US Army psychiatrist, was found guilty of murdering 13 people in a brutal shooting spree at Fort Hood in 2009. While Trump had initially suggested that broadcasting the execution could serve as a deterrent to terrorists, he has now bowed to pressure and cancelled the livestream. However, the immediate families of Hasan's victims will still be allowed to witness the execution in person if they choose to do so. 

The decision is a setback for US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who had backed the plan to livestream the execution as a way of demonstrating the consequences of such heinous crimes. With the Republican Party already on the back foot over the stalemated Iran war, this latest reversal is likely to add to the pressure on Hegseth and the Trump administration.

articles.title: O'Donovan in intensive care after taking ill on Tuesday
articles.rewritten_copy:
MINISTER O'DONOVAN FIGHTS FOR RECOVERY IN INTENSIVE CARE

Minister for Culture, Communications and Sport Patrick O'Donovan is battling back to health in University Hospital Limerick after a shocking seizure at an EU Presidency meeting. The Limerick TD, who has been open about his struggles with epilepsy, was rushed to hospital by ambulance and is now being cared for in intensive care.

As the people of Newcastle West rally around their beloved minister, concerns are being raised about his future in the role. A Fine Gael minister sparked controversy over the weekend by questioning whether O'Donovan is well enough to stay on, prompting a strong response from the minister himself. O'Donovan slammed the anonymous comments as a "slap in the face", and now his friends and colleagues are sending their best wishes for a speedy recovery. With the Ryder Cup coming to Limerick, everyone is hoping O'Donovan will be back to full strength soon.

articles.title: Chambers says 'way forward' on pay talks may come soon
articles.rewritten_copy:
PAY TALKS DEADLOCK: CHAMBERS OFFERS HOPE OF BREAKTHROUGH

Minister for Public Expenditure Jack Chambers has hinted that a breakthrough may be on the horizon in the public sector pay talks, saying he hopes to provide details of a "way forward" shortly. This comes as the country reels from a day of national strike action that saw over 300,000 public sector workers down tools, causing widespread disruption to essential services.

The Labour Party has urged the Government to drop its "arbitrary preconditions" and engage in good faith with trade unions, with Deputy Ged Nash warning that time is running out to avert another day of action next week. Meanwhile, Taoiseach Micheál Martin has said he believes there is a negotiated pathway to a resolution, and has described the Coalition as a "pro-public service" Government. But with unions planning further action if there is no resolution, the clock is ticking for a deal to be done.

articles.title: Drug-related intimidation 'pervasive' in every county
articles.rewritten_copy:
DRUG-RELATED INTIMIDATION EPIDEMIC HITS EVERY COUNTY IN IRELAND

A shocking conference in Portlaoise has revealed the true extent of drug-related intimidation in Ireland, with over 1,000 incidents reported in just two years. Detective Superintendent Sé McCormack warned that these incidents are becoming increasingly violent, with gardaí treating them "extremely seriously". The scourge of drug debt is spreading fear across all counties and communities, with cocaine linked to almost 60% of cases.

The DRIVE project report found that the majority of debts ranged from €1,000 to €4,999, but 39 incidents involved amounts over €20,000. The tragic case of the English family in Waterford, who were murdered in a firebomb attack over a €20,000 drugs debt, highlights the deadly consequences of this intimidation. Sinn Féin TD David Cullinane has called for a review of how threats and requests for help are managed, and how families are supported, while Minister for Foreign Affairs Helen McEntee vowed to "stamp out" this scourge on our society.

Experts warn that drug-related intimidation often begins with verbal harassment, loitering, and surveillance, and can escalate into violence and extortion. Criminologist Triona O'Connor advises victims to "reach out to services" and keep everything as normal as possible, while seeking help from the authorities and community resources. With the Government allocating additional funding to support services, it's time for communities to come together and confront this epidemic head-on.

articles.title: Man who incited hatred of refugees jailed for two years
articles.rewritten_copy:
REFUGEE HATE PREACHER CAGED FOR 2 YEARS

A shocking case of incitement to hatred has ended with a two-year jail sentence for a truck driver who spewed vile abuse at refugees. Graham Carey, 42, from Finglas, made a disgusting livestream on Instagram, labeling refugees "rape-ugees" and calling for violence against them.

This hate-filled rant was made after a local woman alleged she had been sexually assaulted, sparking days of anti-immigration protests. But even when it emerged the alleged attacker was a local white man, the protests continued, fueled by hate and misinformation. Carey's actions were found to be a serious crime, planned and premeditated, by Ms Justice Patricia Ryan.

The judge handed down an 18-month sentence on each count, to run consecutively, but suspended the final year on strict conditions. As he was led away, Carey asked to be put into protective custody, claiming his life was in danger. It's a stark reminder that there are consequences for spreading hate and inciting violence in our communities.

articles.title: Tributes paid to first responders after Waterford attack
articles.rewritten_copy:
TRAGEDY IN WATERFORD: HEROES IN UNIFORM PRAISED AFTER ARSON ATTACK

The Dáil has come together to pay tribute to the brave men and women of our medical and emergency services, who rushed to the scene of the horrific arson attack in Waterford that claimed the lives of four innocent people. Deputy David Cullinane led the praise, thanking these heroes "from the bottom of my heart" for their selfless work in the face of unimaginable tragedy.

Minister Jennifer Carroll MacNeill echoed these sentiments, acknowledging the scale of the tragedy and the exceptional job done by our medics and emergency responders. The bravery and dedication of our ambulance service, in particular, were singled out for praise, with both the deputy and the minister noting that they provide an essential service, often in the most difficult circumstances. As our community comes to terms with this senseless tragedy, we salute the heroes who put their lives on the line every day to keep us safe.

articles.title: Doctors say Pope has recovered well from surgery
articles.rewritten_copy:
POPE LEO XIV BACK TO WORK AFTER CANCER SURGERY

The Pope is making a speedy recovery from surgery to remove a cancerous nodule from his lung, and has already resumed working from his hospital bed. According to his doctors, Pope Leo XIV is getting back to his daily routine, including celebrating Mass with other priests.

The 71-year-old Pontiff's post-operative tests are showing normal levels, and he's even managing to get around independently. His medical team says his recovery is going as expected, but they're still waiting on test results to determine if the cancer has spread.

Meanwhile, it's business as usual for the Pope, who's already looking at documents and planning his upcoming trip to South America. Despite his health scare, Leo is still expected to visit Peru, Uruguay, and Argentina in November. He's set to remain in hospital until at least October 20, but it seems nothing can keep this Pope down for long.

articles.title: Busy M50 slip road closed due to breakdown blockage - live traffic updates
articles.rewritten_copy:
DUBLIN TRAFFIC CHAOS: CITY GRINDS TO A HALT

The streets of Dublin are a war zone today, with crashes, congestion, and breakdowns bringing the city to a standstill. The M50 is a parking lot, with solid traffic southbound from Craobh Chiaráin to the Red Cow and very slow traffic northbound from Dundrum to Lucan.

Out-of-action traffic lights at Hanlon's Corner are adding to the mayhem, while a crash on the Swords Road has blocked the entire road. And if that's not enough, debris on the M2/N2 southbound is causing hazards for drivers, who are being warned to reduce their speed and drive with caution.

Dublin Bus is also feeling the pain, with diversions in place on Clonskeagh Road due to low-hanging wires. Route 11 is being diverted in both directions, with several stops out of action. It's a nightmare out there, folks, so plan your journey carefully and leave plenty of time to get where you're going. As the authorities warn, "some delays to your journey may occur" - that's putting it mildly!

articles.title: Donald Trump issues major update on firing squad execution livestream
articles.rewritten_copy:
TRUMP PUTS FOOT DOWN: NO LIVESTREAM FOR FORT HOOD SHOOTER'S EXECUTION

In a welcome move, US President Donald Trump has confirmed that the execution of Nidal Malik Hasan, the Fort Hood shooter who brutally murdered 13 unarmed soldiers and wounded 32 others, will not be livestreamed. This decision comes after a backlash against the initial proposal to broadcast the event, with many questioning whether it would serve as a deterrent or simply provide a twisted spectacle.

Trump took to his Truth Social platform to announce the decision, stating that while he believes the execution could have served as a strong deterrent, many people would rather not witness Hasan's death. Instead, the families of Hasan's victims will be permitted to witness the execution in person, a move that Trump says will allow them to see "JUSTICE" served. The execution, set to take place on December 3, will be carried out by a military firing squad.

articles.title: Two arrested in connection with Waterford arson attack which killed couple and two children
articles.rewritten_copy:
ARSON HORROR: TWO HELD OVER WATERFORD HOUSE FIRE THAT CLAIMED FOUR LIVES

A man and woman are behind bars as Gardai probe the devastating arson attack that ripped through a home in Waterford's Birchwood estate, leaving four dead and two young children fighting for their lives. The tragic inferno, which engulfed the English family home, has sent shockwaves through the community, with many demanding justice for the victims.

The Gardai are urging anyone with information to come forward, particularly those who may have dashcam footage or witnessed suspicious activity in the area between 4:30am and 5:30am on the morning of the fire. As the investigation continues, the people of Waterford are left to pick up the pieces and wonder how such a heinous crime could occur in their city.

The arrests of the two suspects, a man in his 20s and a woman in her 30s, are a welcome development in the case, but the community will be watching closely to ensure that those responsible are brought to justice. The Gardai have appealed for anyone with information to contact them at Waterford Garda Station or through the Garda Confidential Line.

articles.title: Man accused of murdering his dad and leaving decomposing body in flat for a week
articles.rewritten_copy:
DAD'S BRUTAL MURDER: SON FACES JUSTICE FOR SICKENING KILLING

A chilling tale of murder and deception has unfolded in the Central Criminal Court, where Seth Whelan is on trial for the gruesome killing of his own father, Mick Whelan. The 64-year-old's body was found in a state of decomposition, with a staggering 43 stab wounds and a crushed skull, in the flat he shared with his son in Dublin's Herberton Park.

Prosecutor Anne-Marie Lawlor SC painted a damning picture of the events leading up to the discovery of the body, revealing that Seth Whelan was the only person to enter or leave the flat in the days preceding the murder. The jury will hear how Whelan's demeanour and statements to gardai will be crucial in determining his guilt, as well as the disturbing details of how he allegedly sent messages claiming his father had died while the body lay undiscovered.

The trial will examine the shocking extent of Michael Whelan's injuries, which included two fatal stab wounds and a further 41 inflicted after death. The pathologist's testimony will reveal the horrific nature of the killing, with the victim's skull and face "crushed in". As the trial continues, one thing is clear: justice must be served for this heinous crime.

articles.title: Applications open for new cost rental homes in Swords with one-beds for €1,395 per month
articles.rewritten_copy:
COST RENTAL SCHEME COMES TO SWORDS - BUT IS IT VALUE FOR TAXPAYERS?

A new development in Swords is offering 25 homes for rent at below-market rates, but the question remains - is this the best use of taxpayers' money? The Furzefield development features a range of one, two, and three-bedroom duplex apartments, with rents starting at €1,395 per month for a one-bedroom unit. 

The cost rental scheme is a not-for-profit model, with rents set at least 25% below local market rates, but eligibility criteria apply. The homes themselves boast modern amenities and low-maintenance exteriors, but with applications closing on October 23, those interested will need to act fast. 

As the government continues to invest in affordable housing initiatives, taxpayers will be watching closely to see if schemes like this one deliver value for money. With most homes available from early December, it remains to be seen whether this development will be a success story or a drain on the public purse.

articles.title: 'Shellshocked' - Dublin city food producer The Wild Wok reacts to winning Grow with Aldi 2026
articles.rewritten_copy:
WILD WOK WINS BIG WITH ALDI DEAL

In a major boost for Irish food production, The Wild Wok, a Dublin-based company, has been crowned the winner of Grow With Aldi 2026. This means their locally made gyoza will be stocked in all 167 Aldi stores nationwide for 2027. Founded by Vincent Zhang and Stephen Molloy, The Wild Wok is Ireland's only large-scale producer of gyoza, using traditional Chinese recipes and fresh Irish ingredients.

The company's success is a testament to the power of innovation and hard work. Stephen Molloy described the win as a "very proud moment" and praised the Grow With Aldi programme for helping them scale their business. With their products now available in Aldi stores for just €4.99, Irish consumers can enjoy authentic Chinese-style food made right here in Ireland. This is a win-win for local food producers and taxpayers alike, supporting Irish jobs and the local economy.

articles.title: Behind-the-scenes look shows major progress on Iveagh Markets restoration
articles.rewritten_copy:
IVEAGH MARKETS REVIVAL TAKES SHAPE AFTER YEARS OF NEGLECT

The long-abandoned Iveagh Markets on Francis Street are finally getting the restoration they deserve, thanks to a €9.5 million cash injection from the government. Specialist conservation teams have been working tirelessly to bring the 120-year-old landmark back to life, carefully removing hazardous lead-based paint and restoring the historic steel framework.

As the restoration works progress, fascinating details about the market's construction have come to light, including the names of suppliers from Scotland, England, and Ireland who contributed to its building over a century ago. With the Wet Market steel structure now fully restored, attention is turning to the roof, where the project team aims to retain and reuse as much of the original Westmorland Green slate as possible.

Former Lord Mayor Ray McAdam has welcomed the works, describing the Iveagh Markets as a "cornerstone of Dublin's story" and a symbol of the community's spirit and character. As the project reaches another milestone, it's clear that this iconic landmark is one step closer to being restored to its former glory, and Dubliners can finally look forward to seeing it thrive once again.

articles.title: AD FEATURE: McDonald's and Ronald McDonald House Ireland celebrate almost €230,000 raised on first ever McHappy Day
articles.rewritten_copy:
McHAPPY DAY SMASHES TARGET: McDONALD'S RAISES €230K FOR RONALD McDONALD HOUSE IRELAND

In a staggering display of generosity, McDonald's customers, staff, and suppliers came together to raise a whopping €230,000 for Ronald McDonald House Ireland on the company's first ever McHappy Day in Ireland. The fundraiser, which took place on September 26, saw over 8,700 limited-edition Grimace beanies sold and €1 from every qualifying main meal donated to the charity.

The massive haul will help Ronald McDonald House Ireland continue to support families with children in hospital, providing them with a place to stay and alleviating the financial and emotional burden of being away from their loved ones. With over 5,500 families already helped, this latest boost will ensure the charity can keep up its vital work. As Lauren Schultz, CEO at McDonald's UK & Ireland, said, the success of McHappy Day will help families stay together "at a time when being together matters most".

Joe Kenny, CEO of Ronald McDonald House Ireland, praised the "incredible achievement", saying it would make a real difference to families during "some of the hardest days of their lives". The charity has worked with McDonald's for over 20 years, and this latest fundraiser is a testament to the strength of their partnership.

articles.title: Garda social media accounts hacked by crypto promoters
articles.rewritten_copy:
GARDA SOCIAL MEDIA ACCOUNTS HACKED: CYBER THREAT HITS IRELAND'S CITIZENS

In a shocking breach of security, two official social media accounts run by An Garda Síochána have been hacked by a third-party, sparking widespread concern among the public. The compromised accounts, @GardaTraffic and @GardaInfo, have a massive following of over 900,000 people and were used to promote a cryptocurrency platform.

Gardai have warned citizens not to engage with any suspicious content posted on these accounts, which were accessed via the X platform, formerly known as Twitter. Fortunately, no sensitive data has been exposed, and the breach is limited to the X platform only. The Gardai are currently investigating the incident and working with the X platform to determine how this unauthorized access occurred.

articles.title: Cycling to school up 49% as active travel scheme welcomes 13 new Dublin schools
articles.rewritten_copy:
CYCLING TO SCHOOL SURGES BY 49% THANKS TO SRTS PROGRAMME

The Safe Routes to School programme is yielding impressive results, with cycling to school increasing by a whopping 49% among participating students. This nationwide initiative, which aims to create safer conditions for kids and families walking, wheeling, and cycling to school, has welcomed 13 new Dublin schools into its fold. With 118 schools across the capital now on board, it's clear that this programme is making a real difference.

Minister for Transport Darragh O'Brien has hailed the programme's success, saying it's delivering "real benefits for communities" and helping to create "healthier, more sustainable communities for future generations". And it's not just cycling that's on the up - walking is up 8%, car use is down 10%, and scooting has increased by 17.5%. As the programme continues to expand, it's likely we'll see even more positive changes in the way our kids get to school.

The programme's impact is being felt on the ground, with schools like Pope John Paul II in Malahide reporting calmer traffic conditions and more confident pupils. As Acting Principal Gayle Byrne put it, the new infrastructure has encouraged more kids to cycle or scoot to school, promoting healthier and more active travel habits. With over 600 schools now participating nationwide, it's clear that the Safe Routes to School programme is a recipe for success.

articles.title: Gardaí investigating after man's body found in Co Cork
articles.rewritten_copy:
BODY FOUND ON RIVER BLACKWATER WALKWAY: GARDAÍ PROBE MYSTERY DEATH

In a shocking discovery, a man's lifeless body has been found on a walkway along the River Blackwater, just 3km outside Mallow in north Co Cork, leaving the local community reeling. The grim find was made by unsuspecting walkers sometime after 2pm, sparking a major Garda investigation into the circumstances surrounding the man's death. With the victim's identity still unknown, it's clear that he had suffered injuries, fueling fears of a violent incident. As the scene remains sealed off, the Garda Technical Bureau has been called in from Dublin to scour the area for clues, while the State Pathologist's office prepares for a post-mortem examination. An incident room has been set up at Mallow Garda Station, but the people of Mallow are already demanding answers about how this tragedy occurred on their doorstep. The discovery is a stark reminder of the darker realities that exist in rural Ireland, often overlooked by Leinster House elites more concerned with virtue-signaling than addressing the pressing concerns of working-class communities.

articles.title: U2 announce new world tour - with Irish dates to follow
articles.rewritten_copy:
ELITIST ROCKERS U2 EMBARK ON LAVISH WORLD TOUR WHILE IRISH TAXPAYERS FOOT THE BILL FOR CULTURAL VANTAGE PROJECTS

As the working-class communities of Ireland continue to struggle with the cost-of-living crisis, it's business as usual for the multimillionaire rockers U2, who are gearing up for their 2027 world tour, "Carnaval De Luz presents: The Greatest Show On Earth". This extravagant spectacle will kick off in Mexico City in February, with the band set to perform in "select stadiums" around the globe, courtesy of their lucrative record deals and taxpayer-subsidized arts initiatives. 

The tour, which will feature support from Beck, is a brazen display of the band's wealth and influence, with shows scheduled in Latin America, Europe, and North America. Meanwhile, hard-pressed families in Ireland are left to pick up the tab for the country's bloated cultural sector, which prioritizes vanity projects like U2's lavish tours over essential public services. 

U2's forthcoming 16th studio album, "Carnaval De Luz", is set to drop soon, with the band boasting about their ability to deliver "the best night of anybody's life" - a claim that rings hollow for the countless Irish citizens who can't afford a ticket to their shows, let alone a decent standard of living. The band's statement, replete with pseudo-spiritual mumbo-jumbo, is a testament to their detachment from the everyday realities of ordinary people. 

As the Leinster House elites continue to squander taxpayer cash on indulgent cultural projects, it's clear that U2's world tour is just another example of the systemic rot that pervades Ireland's establishment. While the band rakes in millions from their tour, the working-class communities of Ireland are left to foot the bill for the country's out-of-control spending on arts and culture. It's time for a reckoning - will the Irish people continue to subsidize the lavish lifestyles of elitist rockers like U2, or will they demand a better deal for themselves?

articles.title: Trump's new press secretary scrutinised over credentials
articles.rewritten_copy:
TRUMP'S NEW PRESS SECRETARY EMBROILED IN DEEPENING CREDENTIALS SCANDAL

The White House is facing a mounting crisis over the dubious legal credentials of new press secretary Katie Zacharia, who stumbled through her first day on the job with a disastrous press briefing that raised more questions than answers. A watchdog group has filed a complaint with the State Bar of California, demanding an investigation into whether Zacharia has broken the law by falsely presenting herself as a licensed lawyer. Despite claiming to be an attorney, Zacharia has failed to produce any evidence of passing the bar exam in any US state, with California's state bar confirming it has no record of her holding a license. 

Zacharia's attempts to clarify her credentials have only added to the confusion, with her bizarre claim that she "practised international transaction law" and a vague statement about moving to China when asked about her bar exam results. The Wall Street Journal has revealed that Zacharia sat the California bar exam after graduating from law school but failed to pass, raising serious questions about her fitness for the role of White House press secretary. Meanwhile, President Trump has continued to defend Zacharia, praising her debut performance despite widespread criticism from former White House officials and media commentators. 

The scandal has sparked outrage among hard-working American taxpayers, who expect honesty and transparency from their public officials. Zacharia's apparent deception is just the latest example of the Trump administration's blatant disregard for the truth and its willingness to prioritize loyalty over competence. As the controversy deepens, one thing is clear: Zacharia's credentials scandal is a betrayal of the public's trust and a stark reminder of the systemic rot at the heart of the Washington establishment. 

The fact that Zacharia was able to land a top job in the White House despite her questionable credentials is a damning indictment of the corrupt system that prioritizes connections and ideology over merit and integrity. The American people deserve better than a press secretary who seems more interested in spinning lies than telling the truth. It's time for Zacharia to come clean about her credentials and for the Trump administration to take responsibility for its latest embarrassment. 

The watchdog group's complaint is a welcome step towards holding Zacharia and the White House accountable for their actions. The State Bar of California must now investigate Zacharia's credentials and take swift action if it finds that she has indeed broken the law. Anything less would be a miscarriage of justice and a further erosion of trust in the system. The American people are watching, and they will not tolerate any more deception and corruption from their public officials.

articles.title: Dublin café closed over cockroach infestation
articles.rewritten_copy:
DIRTY KITCHENS EXPOSED: 12 RESTAURANTS SHUT DOWN OVER FILTHY CONDITIONS

In a shocking betrayal of public trust, a dozen restaurants and cafes across Ireland were slapped with closure orders last month due to appalling health and safety breaches. The Hopsack in Rathmines, south Dublin, was one of the worst offenders, with a rampant cockroach infestation at all stages of the lifecycle found in the food service area where ready-to-eat food is prepared. The discovery of dead and live cockroaches in the vicinity of food preparation is a stomach-churning reminder of the systemic rot in some of our country's eateries. 

The Food Safety Authority of Ireland (FSAI) also shut down The Thatch in Co Laois after a dead mouse was found on the floor behind the main bar, and rodent droppings were spotted in the main bar, coffee bar, and kitchen - a clear case of taxpayer-squandering negligence. Centra in Co Cavan was another culprit, failing to implement adequate pest control procedures despite ongoing rat activity. FSAI chief executive Greg Dempsey slammed the closures as "entirely preventable non-compliances" that could have been avoided with proper food safety management systems. 

It's a damning indictment of the lack of accountability in some of our food establishments, and a wake-up call for the Leinster House elites to get tough on those who prioritise profits over people's health. The full list of shame can be found on the FSAI's website, a sobering reminder that some businesses are more concerned with lining their pockets than protecting their customers. As hard-pressed families struggle to make ends meet, it's outrageous that some eateries are still getting away with such blatant disregard for basic hygiene standards.

articles.title: Judge orders Enoch Burke arrest and committal to Mountjoy
articles.rewritten_copy:
TEACHER TRESPASSER THROWN BACK IN JAIL

In a shocking display of contempt for the law, rogue teacher Enoch Burke has been jailed again for brazenly defying a High Court order to stay away from his former school, Wilson's Hospital School. This serial offender has spent over 700 days behind bars since September 2022 for repeatedly trespassing on school grounds, and his latest stunt has left the school community reeling. Despite being released from prison just a few months ago, Burke has continued to flout the law, showing up at the school in late August and causing chaos, including the cancellation of a meeting with parents and first-year pupils.

The school's principal, Noel Cunningham, described the situation as "lamentable" and expressed deep concern about the impact of Burke's behavior on the students and the school's operations. The court heard that Burke had even waited for the security guard to take a break before sneaking into the school, a move that Judge Brian Cregan described as "shocking" and "ignoble". The judge slammed Burke's conduct as "deliberate and flagrant contempt of court" and ordered his immediate arrest and committal to Mountjoy Prison.

This latest development is just the latest chapter in the long-running saga between Burke and the school, which began when the teacher refused to address a student by their preferred pronouns, citing his religious beliefs. The school's attempt to accommodate the student's request was met with belligerent resistance from Burke, who has since become a poster child for extremist ideologies that prioritize individual zealotry over the well-being of students and the rule of law. As the school struggles to maintain order and provide a safe learning environment, Burke's actions have become a stark reminder of the dangers of unchecked ideological fanaticism and the need for swift action to protect vulnerable communities from rogue individuals who think they are above the law.

articles.title: Ireland should prepare for traditional TV switch-off
articles.rewritten_copy:
TV BLACKOUT LOOMING: COMREG WARNS OF DTT SWITCH-OFF

In a stark warning, ComReg has sounded the alarm on the potential switch-off of Digital Terrestrial Television (DTT), leaving thousands of Irish households without access to free-to-air TV channels, including RTÉ's Saorview platform. This impending crisis is a direct result of the establishment's reckless pursuit of online streaming, backed by the Leinster House elites who are more concerned with appeasing big tech than serving the needs of working-class communities. As television consumption increasingly shifts online, ComReg's report reveals a shocking 71% of respondents now use Smart TVs to watch content, while traditional TVs lag behind at 18%. The regulator's research, conducted by Ipsos B&A, surveyed over 1,000 TV decision-makers, exposing the stark reality of Ireland's broadcasting landscape. With the traditional DTT service on the brink of collapse, it's clear that the out-of-touch elites have abandoned the needs of ordinary citizens, prioritizing instead the interests of global tech giants and their own taxpayer-funded gravy train. The future of free-to-air TV hangs in the balance, and it's time for the government to take action to protect the interests of hard-pressed families, not just the privileged few.

articles.title: Ukraine will keep hitting Russian refineries - Zelensky
articles.rewritten_copy:
**UKRAINE BETRAYED: Trump's Treachery Exposed as Zelensky Resumes Strikes on Russian Oil Refineries**

In a shocking rebuke to US President Donald Trump's failed "energy ceasefire," Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has announced that his country will resume targeting Russian oil refineries, exposing the blatant hypocrisy of Trump's Russia-friendly policies. Despite complying with Trump's demands to halt strikes on Russian refineries, Ukraine saw its access to key US military capabilities and intelligence severely restricted, leaving its citizens vulnerable to relentless Russian attacks. Zelensky slammed Trump's actions as a "dangerous" betrayal, warning that the cutting off of intelligence sharing with Kyiv could have devastating consequences for Ukraine's ability to protect its cities from Russian air attacks.

As Russia continues to pound Ukrainian cities with jet-powered drones, Zelensky's decision to restart refinery strikes is a desperate attempt to level the playing field against an enemy emboldened by Trump's weakness. The move comes as EU leaders, tired of Trump's foot-dragging, are stepping up their support for Ukraine, with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz calling for increased funding to plug the gap left by US inaction. Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal went further, declaring that the faster Russia's refineries are destroyed, the better. Meanwhile, Irish charity founder Shane Leahy, on the ground in Kyiv, reported a surge in Russian attacks, with power outages becoming a regular occurrence, leaving hospitals and civilians struggling to cope.

In a stark contrast to Trump's appeasement of Putin, EU leaders are finally taking a stand against Russian aggression, with Merz pushing back against US attempts to interfere with frozen Russian assets, which could be used to fund Ukraine's war effort. As the situation on the ground continues to deteriorate, one thing is clear: Trump's treachery has left Ukraine to face the wrath of Russia alone, and it's up to the EU to pick up the pieces and support Ukraine's fight for survival.

articles.title: Garda social media accounts breached by crypto-hackers
articles.rewritten_copy:
GARDA CYBER SHAMBLES: HACKERS INVADE OFFICIAL ACCOUNTS

In a shocking display of incompetence, two official Garda accounts on the X social media platform have been hacked, leaving hundreds of thousands of followers vulnerable to potential scams and misinformation. The @gardainfo and @gardatraffic accounts, which boast nearly 900,000 followers combined, were compromised, with hackers posting scores of cryptic messages about a dubious cryptocurrency. The location on both accounts was brazenly changed to Amsterdam, the Netherlands, in a clear attempt to deceive the public. 

While Garda Headquarters claims that there has been no unauthorized access to internal systems and no loss of data, this latest debacle raises serious questions about the force's ability to protect itself, let alone the citizens it serves. The fact that the @GardaInfo account is still linked from the official Garda website, despite being hijacked by crypto scammers, is a damning indictment of the Garda's cyber security measures. 

The public is being warned not to interact with any content posted on these compromised accounts, as Gardai scramble to contain the damage and work with X to establish how this breach occurred. This is not just a minor glitch, but a full-blown crisis that exposes the dark underbelly of Ireland's struggling cyber security infrastructure, leaving working-class communities to pick up the pieces of this latest establishment failure.

articles.title: Uisce Éireann CEO defends €118,000 pay rise
articles.rewritten_copy:
**UISCE ÉIREANN CEO'S OBSCENE PAY HIKE EXPOSED**

In a jaw-dropping display of arrogance, Uisce Éireann CEO Niall Gleeson has defended his staggering €118,000 salary increase, bringing his total annual pay to a whopping €391,953. This outrageous rise comes as hard-pressed families struggle to make ends meet and public sector workers fight for modest pay increases. Gleeson's shameless justification for this bloated pay packet is that it was recommended by an independent review, but this only serves to highlight the systemic rot at the heart of our state-owned utilities.

Sinn Féin TD Cathy Bennett rightly slammed Gleeson's pay hike, pointing out the glaring disparity between his lavish raise and the paltry increases being sought by public sector workers. Meanwhile, Gleeson's attempt to justify his salary by citing the utility's supposed "value for money" rings hollow, given the countless constituents struggling with subpar water services, including brown water and lack of access to clean water connections. The fact that Uisce Éireann spends a whopping €4,000 on PR advice before attending Oireachtas committees only adds to the sense of outrage, with Bennett dismissing this as "a joke" and demanding straight answers instead of spin.

The utility's bonus culture is also under fire, with a staggering 97% of staff members receiving bonuses last year, totaling €17.59m. This lucrative bonus system, defended by Gleeson and CFO Chris McCarthy as a "tried and tested market potential that drives performance", only serves to further alienate the working-class communities left behind by Uisce Éireann's failures. As the utility faces a €31m negative revenue withholding due to its inability to meet targets, including leakage reduction, it's clear that Gleeson's priorities are skewed towards lining the pockets of executives rather than serving the people.

The astonishing admission that Uisce Éireann will require almost €50bn in capital investment over the next 25 years to address its chronic water network problems only underscores the catastrophic mismanagement of our state-owned utilities. With €2bn needed annually to fix housing connections, leakages, and other issues, it's clear that the Leinster House elites have abandoned the working-class communities to suffer at the hands of Uisce Éireann's incompetence. As Gleeson boasts about the utility's supposed progress in reducing leaks, the stark reality is that taxpayers will be footing the bill for decades to come, while executives like Gleeson reap the benefits of their own failures.

articles.title: McEntee 'shocked' at UK decision on Sally Rooney books
articles.rewritten_copy:
SHOCKING CENSORSHIP: IRISH AUTHOR SALLY ROONEY'S BOOKS PULLED FROM UK SHELVES OVER PRO-PALESTINE STANCE

In a blatant display of censorship, Sally Rooney's books are being removed from UK shops due to her unwavering support for Palestine Action, a group banned in the UK. Minister for Foreign Affairs Helen McEntee has expressed her shock and plans to raise the matter with her British counterpart, despite being well aware that she cannot comment on another country's laws. This move is a stark reminder of the systemic rot that plagues the UK's establishment, where freedom of speech is being suffocated by the very same elites who claim to champion human rights. Meanwhile, Social Democrats TD Sinéad Gibney has jumped to Rooney's defense, echoing the sentiments of many Irish artists who share her pro-Palestine stance. However, it's clear that this is nothing more than a virtue-signaling exercise, detached from the everyday realities of hard-pressed families struggling to make ends meet. Rooney's decision to continue supporting Palestine Action, despite the group being proscribed as a terrorist organisation in the UK, has led to Faber stopping the supply of her books in the UK, although copies already held by retailers will remain on sale. As the UK Supreme Court prepares to hear an appeal over the ban on Palestine Action, it's becoming increasingly clear that the establishment's hypocrisy knows no bounds, and it's time for the people to take a stand against this blatant assault on free speech.

articles.title: Funeral fundraiser for family who died in arson attack hits 50k as two children remain critical
articles.rewritten_copy:
**DEVASTATING INFERNO: COMMUNITY RALLIES TO SUPPORT FAMILY AFTER SUSPECTED ARSON ATTACK CLAIMS FOUR LIVES**

The people of Waterford have come together in a heart-wrenching display of solidarity to raise a staggering €50,000 for the funeral expenses of Philip and Kim English and their two young sons, Callum and Jayden, who tragically lost their lives in a suspected arson attack on their home in the Birchwood estate. This senseless tragedy has left the community reeling, with two other children still fighting for their lives in hospital. The Gardai have launched a murder investigation and arrested two individuals in connection with the incident, which is believed to have been sparked by a petrol bomb thrown at the house just after 5 am on Tuesday morning. As the family struggles to come to terms with this unimaginable loss, the community's outpouring of support is a testament to the resilience and compassion of the Irish people, who will not stand idly by while innocent lives are lost to mindless violence. The fundraiser, launched by Philip's cousin Sharon, has seen almost 2,000 people donate to support the family in their time of need, with all donations going directly to Patrick English, the grandfather of the deceased and injured children, to cover funeral expenses and support the family through this dark time.

articles.title: Popular south Dublin pizza restaurant shut by inspectors due to rats in kitchen
articles.rewritten_copy:
DIRTY KITCHENS EXPOSED: RATS AND COCKROACHES RUN AMOK IN DUBLIN RESTAURANTS

A shocking wave of food safety failures has rocked Dublin, with a popular south Dublin pizza joint, Pizza Petito, forced to shut its doors after a disgusting infestation of rats was discovered in its kitchen. The Orwell Road restaurant was closed by Environmental Health Officers on September 23 after inspectors found rodent droppings scattered widely across the kitchen, including under a food refrigeration unit, while customers were still being served. This appalling breach of food safety standards is a slap in the face to hard-working taxpayers who expect better from the businesses they support.

Meanwhile, other Dublin eateries, including Marka Cadey 2 and The Hopsack, were also issued closure orders due to separate infestations of cockroaches, highlighting a disturbing trend of neglect and complacency among some food business owners. J2 Sushi & Bento was also temporarily shut down for failing to implement proper food safety procedures, including the handling of high-risk foods like chicken. The Food Safety Authority of Ireland's Chief Executive, Greg Dempsey, warned that these issues are "entirely preventable" with proper management systems in place, but it seems some businesses are more concerned with lining their pockets than protecting their customers' health. It's time for these reckless business owners to be held accountable for their actions and for the authorities to take a tougher stance on enforcing food safety standards to prevent such egregious breaches from happening again.

articles.title: Armed robbery in Balbriggan as Gardai issue description of masked thieves
articles.rewritten_copy:
ARMED ROBBERY ROCKS BALBRIGGAN: THIEVES STRIKE AS GARDAI STRUGGLE TO KEEP UP

In a shocking display of lawlessness, masked thieves carried out a brazen armed robbery in Balbriggan on Saturday, leaving a trail of fear and outrage in their wake. The incident occurred at approximately 9:15pm on October 10 at a business premises in the Old Market Green area, where two men, armed with a suspected firearm, threatened staff and made off with a substantial sum of cash. The Gardai, already under fire for their handling of rising crime rates, are now scrambling to catch the perpetrators, with descriptions of the thieves released in a desperate bid for witnesses to come forward. One of the men was spotted wearing a navy hoodie, navy tracksuit bottoms, white socks, white runners, and a white mask, while the second male was clad in a yellow/beige jacket, navy bottoms, red shoes, and a dark hat. As the people of Balbriggan demand action, the Gardai are urging anyone with information to contact them at Balbriggan Garda Station on 01 666 4500, highlighting the growing concern that our communities are being left to fend for themselves in the face of rampant crime. The incident serves as a stark reminder of the failure of our justice system to protect hardworking citizens, who are being forced to live in fear of violent thugs and opportunistic thieves.

articles.title: Dirty Dublin streets a striking visual metaphor for power of industrial action
articles.rewritten_copy:
DUBLIN DESCENDS INTO FILTHY CHAOS AS PUBLIC SECTOR STRIKE HITS HOME

The streets of Dublin were transformed into a garbage-strewn nightmare yesterday as over 300,000 public sector workers, including the city's waste management and street cleaning teams, went on strike in a bitter pay dispute. The result was a catastrophic collapse of basic services, with overflowing bins, litter-lined streets, and a shocking lack of civic pride on full display. As the city teetered on the brink of chaos, businesses and residents were forced to step in and clean up the mess, highlighting the glaring incompetence of the Council's inability to cope with even a single day of industrial action.

Green Party Councillor Feljin Jose, typically quick to virtue-signal, was forced to confront the harsh reality of a city without its cleaning crews, sharing images of the filthy streets on social media and acknowledging the "staggering" amount of waste generated by Dubliners. However, his feeble attempts to spin the crisis as a justification for more taxpayer-funded spending on public sector wages only served to underscore the systemic rot at the heart of the city's governance. As the strike laid bare the Council's inability to provide basic services, it's clear that the real victims are the hard-pressed taxpayers and working-class communities left to suffer the consequences of establishment incompetence.

The Council's own statement, issued the day before the strike, revealed a shocking lack of preparedness, with only "critical and emergency services" operating and a pathetic plea to the public to "help keep the city clean" by taking litter home. It's a damning indictment of the Council's priorities, which seem to favor ideological posturing over practical problem-solving. Meanwhile, the expansion of the city's cleaning services, including the recruitment of dozens of new staff and the investment of over €12 million in new fleet and specialized waste management vehicles, seems like a drop in the ocean compared to the scale of the crisis unleashed by the strike.

As the city struggles to recover from the chaos, it's clear that the strike has exposed the dark underbelly of Dublin's governance, revealing a system that is more concerned with appeasing public sector unions than serving the needs of its citizens. The people of Dublin deserve better than to be held hostage by the selfish interests of striking workers and the ideological agendas of their political masters. It's! time for a root-and-branch overhaul of the city's governance, one that puts the needs of taxpayers and working-class communities front and center.

articles.title: Workman's Club confirms venue is not closing down following reports
articles.rewritten_copy:
**VENUE SAVED: WORKMAN'S CLUB SHUTS DOWN SHOCK CLOSURE RUMORS**

In a massive relief to Dublin's nightlife scene, the Workman's Club has slammed the brakes on speculation that it was set to close its doors for good. The rumors, which spread like wildfire on social media, claimed the iconic venue would be transformed into a members'-only club, leaving countless fans and regulars in a state of panic. But the Workman's Club has categorically denied these claims, taking to Instagram to set the record straight: "No we are not closing down. Quite the opposite. Seven nights a week until 2:30." The building surrounding the club is indeed undergoing refurbishment, but it's business as usual for the beloved music and events spot. This is a major win for Dublin's working-class communities, who would have been left high and dry by the closure of yet another cultural institution. The Workman's Club remains a beacon of entertainment and nightlife in the city, and its commitment to staying open is a testament to the enduring power of grassroots culture over soulless, elitist gentrification.

articles.title: Glenda Gilson's mum is 'fighting for her life' in hospital as star asks for prayers
articles.rewritten_copy:
HEARTBREAK FOR GLENDAS MUM AS SHE FIGHTS FOR LIFE

In a shocking and devastating turn of events, TV presenter Glenda Gilson's mum, Aileen, has been battling for her life in hospital for a grueling 24 days, leaving her family and friends reeling in shock. The usually vibrant and energetic Aileen, a staple on the red carpet alongside her daughters, has been clinging to life, prompting Glenda to make an emotional appeal for thoughts and prayers. As the family navigates this dark time, Glenda has found solace in the outpouring of support from fans, thanking them for their well wishes and announcing that her mum has finally "turned a corner". Meanwhile, the Leinster House elites and NGO spending rackets continue to squander taxpayer cash on vanity projects, leaving working-class communities like Glenda's to pick up the pieces and face the harsh realities of a crumbling healthcare system. As Glenda praises her mum's incredible health and fitness levels, it's a stark reminder of the catastrophic consequences of a failed establishment policy that prioritizes bureaucratic red tape over people's lives. The Civil Service gravy train rolls on, while hard-pressed families like Glenda's are left to fight for survival, abandoned by the very system that's supposed to support them.

articles.title: Waterford arson attack victim's son combs through CCTV and declares 'I'm not afraid'
articles.rewritten_copy:
**JUSTICE BETRAYED: WATERFORD ARSON ATTACK CLAIMS FOUR INNOCENT LIVES**

In a shocking display of brutal violence, a suspected petrol bomb attack on a family home in Waterford has left four innocent lives lost, including parents Philip and Kim English, and their young sons Callum and Jayden. The senseless tragedy has sparked widespread outrage and calls for justice, with the Gardai urging the public to come forward with any information that may lead to the capture of the perpetrators.

As the investigation continues, John James English, one of Philip's eldest sons, has vowed to speak out for his family and demand justice, refusing to be intimidated into silence. He has been combing through CCTV footage from the weeks leading up to the attack, determined to uncover the truth behind the horrific incident. The English family's tragic fate is a stark reminder of the devastating consequences of violent crime and the urgent need for community cooperation to bring perpetrators to justice.

Chief Superintendent Anthony Pettit has appealed to the public to come forward with any information, stating that there are individuals in the community who know the identities of the killers. The Gardai are urging anyone with information to contact them, and a confidential line has been set up for those who wish to report any details about the attack. As the people of Waterford struggle to come to terms with this heinous crime, one thing is clear: justice must be served, and those responsible must be held accountable for their barbaric actions. The Leinster House elites would do well to take note of the English family's tragic fate and prioritize the safety and security of law-abiding citizens over their obsession with virtue-signaling and soft-on-crime policies.

articles.title: Slow M50 and delays across the city - live traffic updates
articles.rewritten_copy:
TRAFFIC CHAOS HITS DUBLIN AS COMMUTERS FACE DELAYS AND FRUSTRATION

Dublin's roads are a nightmare this morning, with the M1, N3, and N7 all clogged up on approach to the M50, a stark reminder of the city's failing transport infrastructure. The M50 Southbound is a parking lot, with delays stretching from J4 Ballymun to J6 Blanchardstown and again from J9 Red Cow down to J13 Dundrum, a clear example of the systemic rot that has plagued our city's planning for decades. Northbound M50 is slow moving from J9 Red Cow to J7 Lucan, leaving hardworking citizens stuck in traffic, wasting precious time and taxpayer money on fuel.

The usual suspects are also congested, with Swords Road heavy inbound from the flyover at Whitehall, Navan Road backed up from the railway bridge to Ashtown Roundabout, and Phibsborough Road experiencing slight delays from before Harts Corner. Church Street is a mess, backed up to Constitution Hill, while Islandbridge is heavy heading southbound onto Kilmainham. Naas Road is busy along to Bluebell, Stillorgan Road is busy to UCD, and Charlotte Way to Hatch Street is completely jammed, a testament to the Leinster House elites' failure to deliver functional roads and infrastructure for the working-class communities they claim to represent. As Dubliners struggle to get to work, it's clear that the city's transport system is at breaking point, and it's time for a change.

articles.title: Graham Linehan arrest case back under scrutiny after watchdog ruling
articles.rewritten_copy:
MET POLICE BETRAYAL: Scotland Yard Forced to Reopen Probe into Shameful Detention of Father Ted Co-Creator Graham Linehan

In a damning indictment of the Met's blatant disregard for free speech and common sense, a watchdog has slammed the force for its appalling handling of a complaint regarding the detention of Irish writer Graham Linehan. The 58-year-old was hauled off a plane at Heathrow Airport in September 2025, like a common criminal, on suspicion of inciting violence over three posts on X that dared to challenge the radical transgender agenda. After receiving a grovelling apology and a settlement from the Met, Linehan requested a review of the complaint, alleging he was discriminated against due to his gender-critical beliefs - a stark reminder of the toxic climate of intolerance fostered by the progressive elites.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) has now confirmed that the Met's handling of Linehan's complaint was a catastrophic failure, with the force failing to provide satisfactory explanations for the arrest and neglecting to pursue crucial lines of inquiry regarding his bail conditions. The IOPC has directed the Met to reinvestigate the allegations, including the claim of discrimination, in a move that exposes the systemic rot at the heart of our supposedly impartial police force. This shameful episode has sparked outrage among Conservative politicians and renowned author JK Rowling, who have rightly condemned the Met's heavy-handed tactics as a blatant attack on free speech and a stark warning of the dangers of unchecked progressive zealotry.

articles.title: Heavy rain this morning but Met Eireann forecasts good news heading into the weekend
articles.rewritten_copy:
**SETTLED WEEKEND AHEAD BUT DON'T EXPECT ANY RELIEF FROM THE COST-OF-LIVING CRISIS**

As the country braces for a settled and dry weekend, courtesy of high pressure taking over, the real storm is brewing in the pockets of hard-pressed Irish families struggling to make ends meet. Met Eireann's forecast promises a welcome break from the rain, with sunny spells and dry conditions dominating the weekend, but it's little comfort to those feeling the pinch of soaring energy bills and skyrocketing costs of living. Today will start cloudy and wet across Munster, Leinster, and east Ulster, but will gradually clear to mainly dry conditions, with highest temperatures ranging from 12 to 16 degrees.

As the weekend unfolds, expect plenty of sunshine and scattered showers, with cooler temperatures and chilly nights leading to a touch of frost in places. But while the weather may be settling down, the financial storms facing Irish families show no signs of abating. The establishment's failure to address the cost-of-living crisis has left working-class communities feeling abandoned and betrayed, with no relief in sight. The forecast may be looking up, but the future for many Irish families remains uncertain and bleak. With temperatures expected to range from 11 to 14 degrees over the weekend, it's clear that the only thing that's truly "settled" is the establishment's determination to ignore the struggles of ordinary people.

articles.title: Family of murdered Garda Horkan call for public inquiry
articles.rewritten_copy:
**JUSTICE BETRAYAL: HORKAN FAMILY DEMANDS PUBLIC INQUIRY INTO GARDA'S MURDER**

The family of slain Detective Colm Horkan is furious over the lack of accountability six years after his brutal murder in Castlerea, Co Roscommon, and is now demanding a public inquiry to expose the truth. Detective Horkan was fatally shot by Stephen Silver, who had managed to grab the garda's gun from its allegedly faulty holster. The Horkan family has slammed the authorities, citing repeated warnings from protected disclosers that the holster was not fit for purpose, which were blatantly ignored. Revelations from a recent RTÉ Investigates programme have only added to their outrage, with the family condemning the lack of transparency and the silence from the Minister for Justice and other authorities. The family's scathing statement has laid bare the systemic rot within An Garda Síochána, accusing the establishment of covering up the truth and leaving the public in the dark. By refusing a public inquiry, the government is only fueling suspicions of a cover-up, leaving the Horkan family and the Irish people without justice or answers. The family's call for a public inquiry is a stark reminder of the catastrophic failure of the justice system to protect its own and serve the people, rather than shielding the elite from accountability.

articles.title: Gas Networks issue leading to inflated estimated bills
articles.rewritten_copy:
**GAS BILL CHAOS: ESTIMATED BILLS GO THROUGH THE ROOF AS GNI METER READING FIASCO HITS CUSTOMERS**

In a shocking example of bureaucratic bungling, Gas Networks Ireland (GNI) has admitted to a catastrophic failure in their meter reading system, leaving countless gas customers with grossly inflated estimated bills that are many times higher than their usual payments. The scandal, which affects bills covering the period of 9-12 October, has sparked outrage among hard-pressed households already struggling to make ends meet. 

GNI, the State-owned utility responsible for the country's gas network, has apologized for the debacle but has refused to disclose the cause of the problem, merely stating that it has been "identified and fixed". The company is now scrambling to work with gas suppliers and the Commission for Regulation of Utilities (CRU) to correct the affected bills and prevent further financial hardship for customers.

One furious Electric Ireland gas customer received an estimated bill of €665.61 for less than two months, a staggering multiple of their normal bill, despite the period in question being a traditionally low-usage time due to warmer weather. The customer's experience is likely just the tip of the iceberg, with many other suppliers, including Bord Gáis Energy, Energia, and Yuno Energy, also affected by the GNI meter reading fiasco.

In a rare display of customer-centric action, several suppliers have temporarily paused billing and cancelled affected bills to prevent customers from being unfairly charged. However, the fact that this crisis was allowed to happen at all raises serious questions about the competence and accountability of GNI and the broader energy regulatory framework. As the true extent of the damage becomes clear, one thing is certain: the taxpayer-funded bureaucrats at GNI have a lot to answer for.

articles.title: Commercial goods no longer entering Gaza, Israel says
articles.rewritten_copy:
GAZA HUMANITARIAN CRISIS: ISRAEL SLAMS BRAKES ON COMMERCIAL GOODS OVER HAMAS TAX EXTORTION

In a shocking move, Israel has halted the entry of commercial goods into Gaza, citing a blatant tax extortion scheme by Hamas that's crippling the already beleaguered territory. The Israeli military body COGAT announced that Gazan merchants had refused to coordinate with them over the entry of commercial goods, due to a draconian 10,000 shekel fee imposed by Hamas on each truck entering Gaza, as well as a demand for 30% of all sales to be made in cash. Hamas claims the fee is a "voluntary" payment to a national fund, but it's clear that this is just another example of the terrorist organization's blatant exploitation of its own people. With over two-thirds of Gazans facing acute hunger by the end of the year, this latest move will only exacerbate the humanitarian crisis, leaving innocent civilians to suffer while Hamas elitists line their pockets. Meanwhile, Israeli forces have been forced to launch over 1,000 attacks on Gaza in the past 12 months, resulting in the deaths of over 1,400 Palestinians, including at least 300 children, as the territory teeters on the brink of collapse. The international community must wake up to the reality of Hamas's stranglehold on Gaza and demand action to end this senseless suffering.

articles.title: Maduro pleads not guilty to torture charges in US
articles.rewritten_copy:
MADURO'S DESPERATE DENIAL: OUSTED VENEZUELAN DICTATOR PLEADS NOT GUILTY TO TORTURE CHARGES

In a shocking display of arrogance, ousted Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores pleaded not guilty to new US indictment charges accusing them of conspiring to torture political opponents, a brazen attempt to cling to their crumbling legacy of socialist tyranny. The additional charges significantly expand the US criminal case against the power-hungry pair, who previously pleaded not guilty to charges of abusing their power to help drug traffickers ship cocaine, a stark reminder of the systemic rot that defined their 13-year reign of terror.

As they stood shackled and clad in prison uniforms in a Manhattan federal court, Maduro and Flores attempted to feign innocence, with Maduro claiming the accusations against him were "false" and Flores proclaiming she was "completely innocent." However, the damning indictment tells a different story, alleging that Maduro directed Venezuelan officials to torture opposition politicians and military personnel to maintain his grip on power, including a shocking incident in 2014 where he ordered officials to kidnap military personnel and "squeeze them harder" to extract information.

The pair's desperate denials come as no surprise, given their long history of human rights abuses, corruption, and election-rigging, which led to successive US administrations imposing sanctions on top Venezuelan officials and key state companies. Maduro's capture and extradition to the US have been touted as a major foreign policy success by President Trump, who has ramped up cooperation with Venezuela's new leadership, a stark contrast to the failed policies of the socialist elite that prioritized ideology over the welfare of the Venezuelan people.

With a mandatory minimum sentence of 50 years in prison looming over them if convicted, Maduro and Flores are facing the very real possibility of spending the rest of their lives behind bars, a fitting consequence for their heinous crimes against the Venezuelan people. As the trial date approaches, one thing is clear: the era of socialist tyranny in Venezuela is finally coming to an end, and those responsible for its brutal suppression will be brought to justice.

articles.title: Affordable studio spaces for 22 artists open in Dublin
articles.rewritten_copy:
STUDIOS FOR ELITE ARTISTS WHILE WORKING CLASS COMMUNITIES SUFFER
In a move that reeks of elitist pandering, twenty-two new affordable studio spaces for artists have opened on O'Connell Street in Dublin, courtesy of Visual Artists Ireland and funded by Dublin City Council and wealthy investor Mel Sutcliffe's Quanta Capital. This egregious example of taxpayer squandering prioritizes the needs of professional visual artists over the pressing concerns of hard-pressed working-class families struggling to make ends meet. The building, once home to a shoe company, has been refurbished into individual workspaces, a stark reminder of the systemic rot that favors trendy artistic projects over the everyday needs of ordinary citizens. VAI director Noel Kelly gleefully announced plans to roll out more of these projects, further draining the coffers of local authorities and diverting resources away from essential services. Meanwhile, artists like Kathrina Rupit, who had the means to apply for and secure one of these coveted spots, are thrilled to have found a space to pursue their crafts, utterly detached from the harsh realities of the cost-of-living crisis gripping the city.

articles.title: Connections Arts Centre empowers adults with disabilities through art
articles.rewritten_copy:
**ARTISTIC REVOLUTION IN RATHGAR: LOCAL HEROES FIGHTING FOR INCLUSION**

In a groundbreaking initiative, the Connections Arts Centre in Rathgar is empowering adults with intellectual disabilities and neurodivergent individuals to break down barriers and unlock their creative potential. This pioneering project has already supported a staggering 3,406 class participants, providing a safe and accessible space for society's most vulnerable to thrive. Founder and CEO Miriam Spollen's vision is to create a hub where people with disabilities can come together, learn, grow, and connect through the arts, free from fear and judgement.

The centre's remarkable success stories, such as Michael, a young man who discovered his artistic talent through their programmes, are a testament to the power of community and creativity. With 40 artists now supported, the centre is making waves in the local community, engaging with secondary school students and fostering a culture of inclusion. However, despite their achievements, the centre relies heavily on government support and core funding to continue their vital work, highlighting the need for a more sustainable and inclusive approach to funding for social enterprises.

Labour Cllr Fiona Connelly and Independent Cllr Mannix Flynn have praised the centre's work, recognizing its far-reaching benefits for the entire community. However, their calls for increased funding and support must be matched with action, rather than empty rhetoric. The centre's operations manager, Barry Mocke, emphasized the importance of community engagement, stating that their Transition Year programme not only benefits adults with disabilities but also helps secondary school students develop confidence and leadership skills.

As the Connections Arts Centre continues to push boundaries and challenge societal norms, it is essential to acknowledge the systemic barriers that have held people with disabilities back for far too long. The United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities seeks to move people out of segregated campuses and into inclusive community spaces, but more needs to be done to support organizations like the Connections Arts Centre. With its innovative approach to artistic expression and community building, this centre is a beacon of hope for a more inclusive and compassionate society.

articles.title: Urgent recall issued for popular breakfast foods over possible flour beetle presence
articles.rewritten_copy:
**PORRIDGE AND FISH RECALL CHAOS HITS IRELAND**

In a shocking betrayal of consumer trust, certain batches of Ready Brek and Tesco Super Smooth Porridge have been yanked from shelves due to potential contamination with disgusting flour beetles, leaving hard-working families to wonder how such a catastrophe was allowed to happen. The Food Safety Authority of Ireland has finally sounded the alarm, warning that the presence of these vile insects makes the products downright dangerous for human consumption. Meanwhile, shops are scrambling to pull the affected batches, posting recall notices in a desperate bid to prevent further harm to unsuspecting shoppers.

But that's not all - in a separate and equally alarming development, SuperValu has been forced to recall batches of its Smoked Salmon products due to the detection of listeria monocytogenes, a deadly bacterium that can trigger severe complications, particularly among vulnerable groups like expectant mothers, babies, and the elderly. This latest food safety fiasco is a damning indictment of the systemic rot at the heart of Ireland's food regulation system, which is clearly failing to protect the very people it's supposed to serve. articles.title: Elderly father of Waterford blaze victim breaks down at vigil metres from scene
